headline: Early Strike, Suffocating Control: Colombia Overwhelms Ghana
story: Colombia's decisive strike in the 14th minute set the tone for an evening of relentless domination at Kansas City. Quintero and Arias controlled the midfield tempo from the outset, imposing their 4-3-3 on Ghana's reactive 4-1-4-1. The Africans pressed high—4.7 phases to Colombia's 3.2—but without penetration. By half-time, Colombia had amassed eleven shots; Ghana managed just two. Davinson Sanchez's defensive composure meant Ghana rarely threatened the backline.

Colombia's xG of 1.8 against Ghana's 0.26 told the complete story. The winning goal proved sufficient despite second-half profligacy: Quintero's side squandered chances of 0.28 xG (58'), 0.23 xG (81'), and 0.22 xG (90+2'). Ghana's offensive void—zero shots on target—reflected their fundamental lack of answers to Colombia's midfield control and superior ball recovery (13.9 seconds against Ghana's 22.5). Lawrence Ati-Zigi made saves when required, but Thomas Partey's tireless defence could not compensate.

keyMoment.text: Early Colombian strike silenced Ghana's pressing and determined the evening's outcome.

home.verdict: Territorial dominance and clinical efficiency; only that Ghana's press never threatened.
points: Early strike (14') silenced Ghana's high press and kept them at 0.26 xG.
Possession control (55%) through Quintero/Arias mastery forced Ghana into reactive mode.
Ball recovery (13.9s vs 22.5s) exposed Ghana's defensive fragility on turnovers.

away.verdict: High press (4.7 phases) generated no reward; offensive impotence decided it.
points: Zero shots on target reflects systemic isolation; press created no scoring chances.
High press (4.7 phases) exhausted without compensation—xG of merely 0.26 tells the tale.
Ball recovery time (22.5s vs 13.9s) left defence exposed; Partey alone insufficient.

statLine: Ghana's zero shots on target was the match's defining statistic: a clean accounting of total football abdication.
